title: tcp_connect resolves DNS synchronously on the scheduler thread — move resolution onto the completion path
purpose: Ground: `docs/REVIEW-23-07.md` finding M13 (MEDIUM, performance): "`tcp_connect` does blocking DNS on the scheduler thread. `native/tcp_bifs.rs:551` — `to_socket_addrs()` (sync `getaddrinfo`) runs inline before the async submit; a slow/unreachable hostname stalls every process on that scheduler for the resolver timeout — the exact starvation the completion-ring design avoids everywhere else." RE-PINNED AT `a0359a2`: NO DRIFT — `crates/beamr/src/native/tcp_bifs.rs:551-557` is still `fn resolve_host(host: &str, port: u16) -> Result<SocketAddr, Atom>` with `.to_socket_addrs()` at :553, and its single caller is `tcp_connect` at :78 (`let remote_addr = match resolve_host(&host, port) {`), which runs INLINE, on the scheduler worker thread, BEFORE `create_connect_socket` (:82) and before the async `submit_file_io_with_timeout` at :88. `getaddrinfo` is a blocking libc call with no caller-controlled deadline; on a stalled resolver it can hold the thread for seconds. WHAT THAT COSTS: beamr schedulers are OS worker threads each running many processes cooperatively (`Scheduler::new` with `thread_count`); a process wedged inside a native BIF cannot yield, so EVERY process assigned to that scheduler thread stops making progress for the resolver's duration — not just the connecting one. The BIF's own `{timeout, Ms}` option is no defence: it is passed to `submit_file_io_with_timeout` (:96), which only arms AFTER resolution has already returned. HOW EVERY OTHER BLOCKING OPERATION IS ROUTED HERE (the pattern this brief joins): a BIF builds an `IoOp` (`crates/beamr/src/io/ring.rs:17-75`), calls `ProcessContext::submit_file_io_with_timeout` (`crates/beamr/src/native/context/mod.rs:1314-1335`) which registers the host-await suspension BEFORE submitting so a completion cannot race the park (:1326-1328), and returns; the ring executes the work off-scheduler; the completion bridge (`crates/beamr/src/io/bridge.rs:83-106`) wakes the process; the BIF is re-entered, takes the completion via `take_file_io_completion` (`context/mod.rs:1356-1359`), and finishes from the `FileIoContinuation` (`context/mod.rs:142-196`). `tcp_connect` ALREADY uses this shape for the connect itself (:57-102 with `FileIoContinuation::Connect { fd }` at :93 and `finish_connect` at :326-349); resolution is the one step that never joined it. AND THE RING ALREADY HAS A LANE FOR NON-KERNEL BLOCKING WORK: on Linux, `build_entry` executes filesystem operations INLINE on the io_uring worker thread and completes them through a Nop SQE via `ready_result` (`crates/beamr/src/io/uring.rs:379-401`, helper at :541-546) precisely because io_uring has no opcode for them; on non-Linux, `execute_op` (`crates/beamr/src/io/thread_pool.rs:262-300`) runs everything on a pool worker. Name resolution is exactly that class of work.
task:
DESIGN STANCE (decided). Resolution becomes a completion-ring operation with its own continuation stage, so the scheduler thread never blocks on `getaddrinfo`. Four moving parts, plus one seam that exists solely so the defect is testable before and after.

D1 THE RESOLVER SEAM COMES FIRST, AND IT IS WHAT MAKES RED-FIRST POSSIBLE. A stalled resolver cannot be produced deterministically from a real hostname without wall-clock games, and wall-clock sleeps are forbidden as the test mechanism. So R1 introduces ONE resolver seam — a new `crates/beamr/src/io/resolve.rs` owning the real `to_socket_addrs` logic plus a `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]` injectable override (the established house pattern: `scheduler/execution.rs:837-852`, `scheduler/mod.rs:453-480`, `distribution/mod.rs:253`). In R1 the seam changes NOTHING about where resolution runs — `tcp_bifs::resolve_host` simply delegates to it, still inline, still on the scheduler thread — and that is the point: the SAME injection point is valid before and after the fix, so the red test and the green test are the same test. The seam lives under `io/` rather than `native/` because after R2 it is the RING that calls it, and because `tcp_bifs` already depends on `crate::io` (`tcp_bifs.rs:10-11`).

D2 A NEW RING OPERATION. Add `IoOp::ResolveHost { host: String, port: u16 }` (`io/ring.rs:17-75`) and `IoResult::Resolved(SocketAddr)` (:110-139); both enums derive `Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq` and both new payloads satisfy that. On non-Linux, `execute_op` (`thread_pool.rs:262-300`) gains the arm and runs it on a pool worker. On Linux, `build_entry` (`uring.rs:294-458`) gains the arm using the EXISTING `ready_result` escape hatch (:541-546) that `ListDir`/`MakeDir`/`DelFile`/`DelDir`/`Rename` already use — i.e. resolution runs on the ring thread and completes via a Nop SQE. HONEST NOTE, to be carried in the code comment and the handoff: `ready_result` runs the work on the RING thread, so a stalled resolver stalls that ring's other submissions even though it no longer stalls any scheduler thread. That is a strict improvement, it is parity with the five filesystem operations already routed that way, and it is the M13 acceptance ("a slow resolver must not block an unrelated PROCESS on the same SCHEDULER") met exactly. Moving the `ready_result` family onto a dedicated blocking executor is a separate, larger lane — name it in the handoff as a board candidate (suggested id BEAMR-URING-READY-RESULT-OFFLOAD), do not build it here.

D3 THE COMPLETION MECHANISM IS THE EXISTING ONE, AND NO-POLLING BINDS IT. The resolve op is submitted through `submit_file_io_with_timeout` exactly like the connect op, so the process PARKS and is woken by the completion bridge when the CQE/worker result arrives. NO new wait loop, NO progress check, NO `pending_count` polling, NO retry timer, NO `thread::sleep` anywhere in the resolution path. If the builder finds itself wanting to ask "has the resolution finished yet?", the design has gone wrong.

D4 TWO-STAGE `tcp_connect`, WITH A LITERAL-IP FAST PATH. `FileIoContinuation` (`context/mod.rs:142-196`) gains a `ResolveConnect` variant carrying what stage two needs: the parsed `ConnectOptions` (`tcp_bifs.rs:460-465`, already `Copy + Clone + Debug`) and the deadline bookkeeping. `tcp_connect` (:57-102) becomes: parse args; if the host parses as a literal `Ipv4Addr`, take the FAST PATH — no resolver, no ring round trip, socket created and `IoOp::Connect` submitted exactly as today; otherwise submit `IoOp::ResolveHost` with the `ResolveConnect` continuation and return. On re-entry with a `ResolveConnect` completion, build the socket from the carried options and submit `IoOp::Connect` with the existing `FileIoContinuation::Connect { fd }`; on re-entry with a `Connect` completion, `finish_connect` (:326-349) is unchanged. The literal-IP fast path is not an optimisation flourish: it keeps the three existing `tcp_connect` unit tests (`native/tcp_bifs_tests.rs:421-497`, all of which use `b"127.0.0.1"`) valid UNMODIFIED, which is the cheapest possible regression wall on this change.

D5 TIMEOUT ACCOUNTING SPANS BOTH STAGES. Today `{timeout, Ms}` arms one suspension (:88-97). With two stages a naive implementation gives each stage the full `Ms`, doubling the worst case. The continuation therefore carries a deadline captured at first entry, and stage two arms with the REMAINING time; if nothing remains when the resolve completes, the BIF returns `{error, timeout}` without creating a socket. The zero-timeout early return (:74-76) and the `receive_timeout_expired` check at entry (:61-65) keep their current behaviour. The exact representation (carried `Instant` vs carried remaining-millis) is the builder's call, stated in the handoff.

D6 SCOPE FENCE. Only `tcp_connect` is in scope. `udp_bifs`, the distribution connector, `tcp_listen`/`tcp_accept`/`tcp_send`/`tcp_recv` and any other `to_socket_addrs` user are untouched — a repo-wide grep at the pin shows `to_socket_addrs` occurring exactly once, at `tcp_bifs.rs:553`, so this brief closes the whole M13 surface without widening. IPv6 is out of scope: `resolve_host` filters to `SocketAddr::is_ipv4` (:555) and `create_connect_socket` opens `AF_INET` (:506); that stays exactly as it is.

requirements.title: Resolver seam plus the RED probe: a stalled resolver starves an unrelated process on the same scheduler
requirements.spec: Per D1: create `crates/beamr/src/io/resolve.rs` holding the real resolution (the current `to_socket_addrs` + `is_ipv4` filter + first-address selection, moved verbatim from `tcp_bifs.rs:551-557`) behind `pub(crate) fn resolve_host(host: &str, port: u16) -> io::Result<SocketAddr>`, with a `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]` injection hook allowing a test to install a resolver that BLOCKS until the test releases it (a gate the test owns, not a sleep). `tcp_bifs::resolve_host` delegates to it with NO change in where or when it runs. Then a new integration test `crates/beamr/tests/tcp_connect_resolver_starvation.rs`: start a `Scheduler` with `thread_count: Some(1)`; install a gated resolver; drive `erlang:tcp_connect/3` against a NON-literal hostname from one process; from a second process on the same scheduler, perform a trivial computation and signal completion; assert the second process's signal is observed on a channel with a watchdog deadline (the `run_bounded` shape at `crates/beamr/tests/function_clause_e2e.rs:50-66`), and only THEN release the resolver gate and assert the connect leg finishes.
acceptance: Pre-fix RED: with the resolver gated, the unrelated process NEVER runs — the watchdog `recv_timeout` returns `Err(Timeout)` because the single scheduler thread is inside `getaddrinfo` — recorded as the fail-first evidence

Post-fix GREEN: the unrelated process completes while the resolve op is still outstanding; the ordering is asserted (second process observed BEFORE the gate is released), so the proof is a happens-before relation and NOT a wall-clock measurement

NO SLEEPS AS MECHANISM: the only `Duration` in the test is the watchdog deadline, documented in the file header as the OBSERVER (per the `function_clause_e2e.rs` precedent); the resolver gate is a channel/condvar the test controls

The seam is behaviour-neutral in R1: with no injected resolver, `tcp_connect` resolves exactly as it does at `a0359a2`, and the three existing `tcp_connect` unit tests (`native/tcp_bifs_tests.rs:421-497`) pass unmodified

The injection hook is `test-support`/`cfg(test)` gated and contributes nothing to a default build; the integration test reaches it through the existing dev-dependency self-dep (`crates/beamr/Cargo.toml` dev-dependencies, `features = ["test-support"]`)
Ten consecutive isolated runs are stable in both directions

requirements.title: ResolveHost becomes a completion-ring operation on both backends
requirements.spec: Per D2: add `IoOp::ResolveHost { host: String, port: u16 }` to `crates/beamr/src/io/ring.rs:17-75` and `IoResult::Resolved(SocketAddr)` to :110-139, each with the doc comment the neighbouring variants carry. Non-Linux: `execute_op` (`io/thread_pool.rs:262-300`) gains the arm calling `crate::io::resolve::resolve_host`. Linux: `build_entry` (`io/uring.rs:294-458`) gains the arm using `ready_result` (:541-546), with the D2 honesty comment stating that the work runs on the ring thread, why that is the same posture as the five filesystem ops immediately above it, and what it does and does not buy. `io_completion_to_term` (`io/bridge.rs:148-167`) gains its arm for the new `IoResult` so the exhaustive match still compiles without a catch-all.
acceptance: Every `IoOp`/`IoResult` match in the tree compiles without adding a `_ =>` arm — the exhaustive-match discipline is what forces a future backend to declare how it resolves (list the swept sites in the handoff; `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` is the discovery mechanism)

Both backends produce a completion for a successful resolve and for a failing one, and the failure maps through the existing errno/`io::Error` path so `{error, Reason}` reasons stay in the established vocabulary (`io/mod.rs:117-145` `errno_to_atom`, `tcp_bifs::error_reason`)
`IoOp` and `IoResult` still derive `Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq`; the `MockRing` implementations in the test modules (`native/tcp_bifs_tests.rs:23-53`, `io/bridge.rs:233-258`) still compile
No timed wait, no retry, no progress check is added to either executor (NO-POLLING)
ZERO new `#[allow]`; no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside `cfg(test)`

requirements.title: tcp_connect becomes two-stage, with a literal-IP fast path and a deadline that spans both stages
requirements.spec: Per D4/D5: add `FileIoContinuation::ResolveConnect { .. }` to `crates/beamr/src/native/context/mod.rs:142-196` carrying `ConnectOptions` and the deadline bookkeeping (the enum is `#[cfg(feature = "threads")]` and derives `Clone, Debug`, so the payload must too — `ConnectOptions` at `tcp_bifs.rs:460-465` already derives `Copy, Clone, Debug`). Rework `tcp_connect` (`tcp_bifs.rs:57-102`): literal-`Ipv4Addr` hosts take the existing single-stage path unchanged; hostnames submit `IoOp::ResolveHost` with the new continuation. Add the stage-two handler that builds the socket via the untouched `create_connect_socket` (:503-515) and submits `IoOp::Connect` with `FileIoContinuation::Connect { fd }`. `finish_connect` (:326-349) gains an EXPLICIT arm for the new variant (returning the existing unexpected-continuation error) rather than relying on its pre-existing `_ =>` at :333 — no NEW catch-all is introduced and the old one is not widened.
acceptance: The three existing `tcp_connect` unit tests (`native/tcp_bifs_tests.rs:421-497`) pass UNMODIFIED — they all use the literal `127.0.0.1`, so the fast path preserves them exactly; if any needs editing, the fast path is wrong

New unit tests in the same file cover the hostname path against the `MockFileIoFacility`: first call submits `IoOp::ResolveHost` and suspends; a pushed `Resolved` completion causes an `IoOp::Connect` submission with the resolved address and a `Connect` continuation; a pushed resolve FAILURE returns `{error, Reason}` and creates NO socket (no fd leak)

Timeout spans both stages: with `{timeout, Ms}`, the total wait across resolve+connect does not exceed `Ms`; a resolve that consumes the budget returns `{error, timeout}` without creating a socket; the zero-timeout early return (:74-76) is unchanged
No fd is created before resolution succeeds, so a failed or timed-out resolve cannot leak a descriptor
Capability, arity and registration are untouched (`register_tcp_bifs` :25-54, `Capability::ExternalIo`), and the BIF's success/failure term shapes are byte-identical to today
ZERO new `#[allow]`; no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside `cfg(test)`; no new `_ =>` arm anywhere in the diff

requirements.title: The starvation wall becomes permanent, and the scheduler-thread block is mechanically excluded
requirements.spec: Promote R1's probe to a permanent wall in the suite (it is the M13 negative assertion: no scheduler thread ever blocks on name resolution), and add a mechanical guard: a grep wall asserting `to_socket_addrs` occurs in `crates/beamr/src/` only inside `io/resolve.rs`, so a future BIF cannot quietly reintroduce inline resolution on a scheduler thread.
acceptance: The wall is falsifiable: routing resolution back inline in `tcp_connect` makes both halves red — the starvation test times out and the grep wall reports a second `to_socket_addrs` site
Fail-first recorded-and-reverted for both halves

The grep wall runs over the source tree (not over a diff), so it cannot go vacuously green — and if it is ever expressed against a diff it must use `git -c diff.external= diff --no-ext-diff` per the house DIFF-GREP TRAP
The wall's file header states what it pins and why, in the `timer_resident_cost.rs` methodology style

boundaries: NO-POLLING IS LOAD-BEARING AND FORBIDS, SPECIFICALLY: (a) any loop that asks whether resolution has finished (`pending_count`, a completion-drain retry, a `try_recv` spin); (b) any `thread::sleep`, `yield_now` or backoff in the resolve path; (c) any timer whose job is to re-check the resolve op; (d) a resolver worker that wakes periodically. Completion delivery is the EXISTING park-and-wake through `submit_file_io_with_timeout` (`context/mod.rs:1314-1335`, suspension registered before submission at :1326-1328) and the completion bridge; the process is TOLD its result. The test's watchdog deadline is an observer, not a mechanism.

NO GETADDRINFO ON A SCHEDULER THREAD, EVER — that is the whole finding. A fix that keeps resolution inline and merely bounds it (an alarm, a timeout thread, a cached negative result) does not satisfy this brief.

SEMANTICS FROZEN: `erlang:tcp_connect/3`'s argument shapes, its `ok`/`{ok, Fd}`/`{error, Reason}` term shapes, its reason atoms, its capability (`ExternalIo`), its IPv4-only behaviour (`is_ipv4` filter at `tcp_bifs.rs:555`, `AF_INET` at :506) and `finish_connect`'s existing arms are unchanged. This moves WHERE resolution runs, not WHAT the BIF returns.

SCOPE FENCE: only `tcp_connect`. `to_socket_addrs` occurs exactly once in `crates/beamr/src/` at the pin; do not widen into `udp_bifs`, distribution, or the listener/accept/send/recv BIFs. No IPv6, no resolver cache, no happy-eyeballs, no multi-address fallback (the current code takes the first IPv4 address and that behaviour is preserved).

WASM32: every file this brief touches is native-only — `pub mod io` is `#[cfg(feature = "threads")]` (`lib.rs:23-25`), `pub mod tcp_bifs` is `#[cfg(feature = "net")]` (`native/mod.rs:80-81`), and `FileIoContinuation` plus the whole file-IO facility are `#[cfg(feature = "threads")]` (`context/mod.rs:143`, :199-205). CONFIRMED: nothing here reaches the cooperative wasm32 closure, the beamr-wasm 80-test count and its three CI carriers are untouched. `native/context/mod.rs` is nonetheless a shared file compiled in both closures, so both wasm32 check legs must be run and stay green after the new variant lands.

ZERO new `#[allow]`; no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside `cfg(test)`; no new `_ =>` catch-all arms (the new `IoOp`/`IoResult`/`FileIoContinuation` variants must be compile-forced everywhere they are matched); `crates/beamr/src/loader/encode/**` untouchable; NO NEW CONFIG KNOBS — no resolver pool size, no resolver timeout setting, no cache TTL.

OUT OF SCOPE, RECORD DO NOT FIX: the `ready_result` family runs on the io_uring ring thread (D2) — board candidate BEAMR-URING-READY-RESULT-OFFLOAD; and this brief must not be blocked on it, since meeting M13 only requires getting off the SCHEDULER thread.
verification: Full release battery at the final head: the committed 5-leg `gates.json` run (`fmt`; fresh `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` with `cargo clean -p beamr` and the Compiling line captured; `wasm32-check`; `wasm-tests` with the exact 80-passed carrier unchanged; `tests` workspace-wide), plus the cooperative wasm closure leg (`cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p beamr --no-default-features --features cooperative,json --locked`), a `--features test-support` build leg (the new hook must not break a normal build or a test-support build), and a prohibition grep sweep run through `git -c diff.external= diff --no-ext-diff`. PLATFORM HONESTY: this box is darwin, so a local run exercises the `thread_pool` executor arm and only COMPILES the io_uring arm; the Linux `ready_result` arm needs a Linux run and the handoff must state which legs ran where. Isolation: `tcp_connect_resolver_starvation` 10x, plus the `native::tcp_bifs_tests` module 10x. FAIL-FIRST, recorded-and-reverted: (a) route resolution back inline in `tcp_connect` -> R1/R4 starvation wall times out and the grep wall reports a second site -> restore; (b) give stage two the full `{timeout, Ms}` instead of the remainder -> the R3 two-stage timeout test goes red -> restore; (c) remove the literal-IP fast path -> the three pre-existing `tcp_connect` unit tests go red -> restore. PIN-SHIFT RE-VERIFY at the actual build base (pinned at `a0359a2`): re-read `native/tcp_bifs.rs:57-102`, :326-349, :460-501, :503-515, :551-557, :678-684; `native/context/mod.rs:142-196`, :1314-1359; `io/ring.rs:17-75`, :108-139, :151-182; `io/uring.rs:294-458` (especially `ready_result` at :541-546 and the fs arms at :379-401); `io/thread_pool.rs:262-300`; `io/bridge.rs:83-106`, :148-167; and re-run `grep -rn to_socket_addrs crates/beamr/src` to confirm the single-site claim still holds. Handoff carries: the deadline representation chosen (D5), the swept exhaustive-match site list, the resolver-seam hook shape, and the BEAMR-URING-READY-RESULT-OFFLOAD board candidate.
